items.title: Police dismantle Kratos phishing platform, arrest developer
items.description: Authorities in Germany and the U.S. dismantled the central infrastructure of Kratos, a phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) platform with global reach, and its developer was arrested in Indonesia. [...]

items.title: FakeGit campaign uses 7,600 GitHub repos to push SmartLoader malware
items.description: A large-scale operation dubbed 'FakeGit' is pushing SmartLoader and StealC malware through 7,600 malicious GitHub repositories that accumulated more than 14 million downloads. [...]

items.title: Ransomware Is Accelerating, But It's Not Because of AI
items.description: Researchers pointed to fragmentation of the ransomware ecosystem, the emergence of new attackers, and expansion of attacks on less defended organizations.

items.title: Using LLMs to Find and Prioritize Vulnerabilities Is No Easy Task
items.description: The latest large language models have high false-positive rates and fail to take into account the context of scans, leading to more work for AppSec professionals.

items.title: Critical SharePoint RCE flaw exploited to steal machine keys
items.description: Hackers are actively exploiting the critical CVE-2026-50522 vulnerability in Microsoft SharePoint to steal machine keys and maintain access even after affected servers are patched. [...]

items.title: Hackers Turn Fake Games Into Multi-Stage Infostealers That Steal Passwords and Crypto Wallets
items.description: Criminals are using fake game downloads to slip a sophisticated information stealer onto Windows computers. The campaign hides behind supposed games, mods, cracks, and other software, exploiting the trust and urgency around free or hard-to-find downloads. items.title: Qilin Ransomware Claims 1,358 Victims as Global Attacks Reach New Record
items.description: Qilin ransomware has grown from a fast-moving criminal operation into one of the most visible threats in the global extortion landscape. The group encrypts systems and steals data, then pressures victims with the risk of public leaks. Its campaigns have disrupted organizations across sectors and countries, creating both operational and reputational damage. Ransomware groups increasingly […] The…

items.title: Anubis ransomware claims Coca-Cola Fairlife attack, threatens data leak
items.description: The Anubis ransomware gang has claimed responsibility for the cyberattack on Coca-Cola's Fairlife dairy subsidiary, threatening to publish allegedly stolen corporate data unless the company pays a ransom. [...]

items.title: Apple Fixes Hide My Email Bug That Exposed Real Addresses in Mail Logs
items.description: Apple has moved to address a security flaw in its Hide My Email service that enabled users' real email addresses to be unmasked, effectively undermining the feature's privacy guarantees. 404 Media reported Tuesday that a fix for the issue was deployed by Apple on July 3, 2026, after more than a year, when it was disclosed to the company by Tyler Murphy, co-founder of EasyOptOuts. items.title: Trump Orders Defense Contractors to Map Software, Suppliers Across Critical Supply Chains
items.description: New executive order calls for end-to-end visibility into defense supply chains, including software dependencies, foreign ownership and cyber-related supplier risks. items.description: The open-weight Antares models are designed to pinpoint known vulnerabilities in codebases faster and at a fraction of the cost of larger AI models. The post Cisco Launches Low-Cost AI Models for Source Code Security appeared first on SecurityWeek.

Sold as a subscription crypter for as much as $2,000 a month, it wraps malicious programs so security tools struggle to inspect, block, and trace them. items.title: Hackers Hijack 20+ Government Websites to Deliver Malware Through Trusted Links
items.description: An active malware campaign, dubbed PhantomEnigma, that abuses compromised Brazilian government infrastructure to distribute malicious payloads while evading detection. The operation has hijacked at least 20 official “.gov.br” municipal and police portals, using them as trusted delivery points for malware targeting banking and public-sector organizations. items.title: Critical wp2shell WordPress flaws exploited to install webshells
items.description: Hackers are exploiting the "wp2shell" critical vulnerability suite (CVE-2026-63030 and CVE-2026-60137) affecting WordPress Core to deploy persistent webshells and install malicious plugins on affected servers. [...]

items.title: Trump’s AI Safety Chief Quits Just Three Months After Taking Charge
items.description: Chris Fall has resigned as the director of the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI), leaving the Trump administration’s AI safety organization without a permanent leader just three months after his appointment. items.title: AWS Kiro Flaw Let a Poisoned Web Page Rewrite Its Config and Run Code
items.description: Hidden text on a web page was enough to make Kiro, AWS's agentic coding IDE, rewrite its own configuration file and run an attacker's code on a developer's machine, with no approval step able to stop it. items.description: AI-generated code introduces 15 vulnerabilities on average per codebase, but the actual risk depends on framework pairing more than the model used.
